reasons: No test is visible in this packet.
The file is short and deterministic, which makes testing straightforward.

terms.meaning: How much a moment could change the result of the match. High leverage means the decision matters a lot.
One tenth of a list. Top decile means the top ten percent of moments by leverage.
A limit on how many picks can share one feature, such as one season or one team.
A simple way to find a value at a given percentage of a sorted list, taking the first value that reaches that percentage.

sections.name: File setup, Phase
sections.title: File setup and phase names
sections.what: Describes the file's purpose and defines the three game phases: powerplay, middle and death.
sections.why: The header explains that the selection is about leverage and diversity, and the phase names come from cricket usage.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new phase name would require every cap to include it, or the selection will fail.

sections.name: phaseOf, Candidate
sections.title: Phase labels and candidate shape
sections.what: Labels a moment as powerplay, middle or death using how many balls are left: more than 84 is powerplay, 24 or fewer is death, and everything else is middle. It also defines the shape of a candidate moment.
sections.why: The doc comment defines powerplay as the first six overs and death as the last four, which matches these thresholds.
sections.watch_out: The thresholds assume a full 20-over innings. A shortened match would give the wrong phase.

sections.name: quantile
sections.title: Value at a percentage point
sections.what: Returns the value at a given percentage of a list, using the nearest-rank method, and refuses an empty list.
sections.why: Likely reason: used to find the leverage cut-off for the top decile, which the header names.
sections.watch_out: The function sorts a copy of the list each time, so calling it inside a loop over large data will be slow.

sections.name: diversify
sections.title: Greedy diversified pick
sections.what: Goes through candidates from highest leverage down. It keeps a candidate only if its match, season, phase, teams and answer caps all allow it, and stops once enough are chosen.
sections.why: The doc comment describes the rules: one moment per match, plus caps on season, phase, team and answer, so no fixed answer scores well.
sections.watch_out: Because it is greedy, an early high-leverage pick can block later picks. The result is fast and stable but not guaranteed to be the best possible mix.

summary: Chooses the most important moments of the season for the decision lab, spreading them across matches, seasons, phases, teams and answers so no single type dominates.
purpose: Produces a varied shortlist of high-leverage moments, so the lab does not show many near-identical situations.
why: The header says the selection is top-decile leverage, diversified by match, season, phase and team. The reason for the diversity rules is stated in the doc reference rather than the code.
how: 1) Labels each moment with a phase from the balls left. 2) Sorts candidates by leverage, highest first, with ties broken by identifier. 3) Walks down the list, skipping any candidate that would break a cap. 4) Stops when enough moments are picked. Also provides a quantile helper.
inputs: Candidate moments with identifier, match, season, phase, teams, leverage score and optional answer, plus caps for each diversity rule.
outputs: A shortlist of candidate moments, with fewer than requested if the caps cannot all be met. Also a phase label for a ball count and a quantile value.
risks: Caps that are too tight return a short list without any error. A moment with a phase name not in the caps will fail the lookup. Ties in leverage are resolved by identifier, so the order is stable but may not be meaningful.
debug: If the list is shorter than expected, check each cap against the candidates, especially the answer cap and the per-team cap. If phases look wrong, check the balls-left value, since the powerplay threshold is more than 84 balls.
